topic: Vijayanagara and Bahmani Kingdoms of Indian History
description: During the 14th century, two powerful empires emerged in South India: Vijayanagara, a great Hindu empire, and the Bahmani Kingdom, an Islamic sultanate. Their history is marked by significant cultural achievements, administrative innovations, and a continuous struggle for control over the fertile Raichur Doab.

sections.title: Foundation and Dynasties of the Vijayanagara Empire
sections.description: The Vijayanagara Empire was ruled by four successive dynasties over a period of about three centuries, shaping the political landscape of South India.

key_concepts.explanation: The empire was ruled chronologically by four dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu.

historical_events.significance: Founded by the brothers Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty, with the blessings of the sage Vidyaranya.
The greatest ruler of the Tuluva dynasty, under whom the empire reached its military and cultural zenith.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: On the southern banks of the Tungabhadra River
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Served as the magnificent capital of the Vijayanagara Empire and is currently a recognized UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: The fertile land between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The primary bone of contention and cause for continuous military conflicts between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani empires.

sections.title: Administration, Economy, and Culture of Vijayanagara
sections.description: The empire was highly noted for its decentralized yet robust administrative structures, flourishing trade, and monumental architecture.

key_concepts.explanation: A key feature of provincial administration where military commanders (called Amara-nayakas) were granted land tracts in exchange for maintaining troops and rendering military service to the king.
The village administration system where a body of 12 functionaries (Ayagars) managed the socio-economic affairs of the village.

key_associations.extra_info: An outstanding literary masterpiece written in the Telugu language dealing with statecraft and political maxims.
A collective term for the eight great Telugu poets in his court, prominently featuring Allasani Peddana and Tenali Ramakrishna.

important_facts.fact: The standard gold coin of the Vijayanagara Empire was known as the 'Varaha' or 'Pagoda'.
Vijayanagara architecture is distinguished by the addition of 'Kalyana Mandapas' (marriage halls) and towering 'Gopurams' (gateway towers) to temple structures.

sections.title: The Bahmani Kingdom: Foundation and Key Rulers
sections.description: The Bahmani Kingdom was the first independent Islamic state in the Deccan, acting as a major political and cultural counterweight to Vijayanagara.

historical_events.significance: Founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) during the reign of the Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
Mahmud Gawan was a brilliant Prime Minister; his unjust execution sparked factionalism and initiated the rapid decline of the empire.

key_concepts.explanation: The Bahmani kingdom was administratively divided into major provinces called 'Tarafs', and the provincial governors were titled 'Tarafdars'.

important_facts.fact: Firuz Shah Bahmani founded the city of Firuzabad on the banks of the Bhima River and built an observatory in Daulatabad due to his deep interest in astronomy.

sections.title: Deccan Sultanates and the Battle of Talikota
sections.description: Following the disintegration of the Bahmani Kingdom, it split into five distinct Deccan Sultanates, which eventually united against Vijayanagara.

key_associations.extra_info: Founded by Yusuf Adil Khan. Famous for the Gol Gumbaz, the mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah.
Founded by Quli Qutb Shah. Famous for building the iconic Charminar in Hyderabad.
Founded by Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah.
Founded by Fath Ullah Imad Shah.

historical_events.significance: A combined coalition of the Deccan Sultanates decisively defeated the Vijayanagara army. Rama Raya was killed, and the glorious city of Hampi was sacked and destroyed.

sections.title: Key Foreign Travelers to Vijayanagara
sections.description: Numerous foreign merchants, ambassadors, and travelers visited the Vijayanagara Empire, leaving behind rich historical chronicles of its immense wealth and administration.

key_associations.extra_info: Visited in 1420 AD and provided a detailed account of the city's elaborate fortifications and festivals.
An envoy who famously wrote that he had 'neither seen nor heard of any place equaling' Vijayanagara in the world.
Compared the grandeur and size of Vijayanagara to Rome, highly praising its advanced irrigation and prosperous markets.
A horse trader who provided detailed insights into the history of the foundation of the city and social customs like Sati.
